chunks: Sa'd, from Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about medicine when it is on a man's hand: is it sufficient for him to wipe over the coating of the medicine? He said: “Yes, it is sufficient for him to wipe over it.”

key_terms.الدَّوَاءِ: medicine or medicinal substance applied to the body
key_terms.طَلَى: the coating or layer spread over something
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ: over it, meaning over the medicinal coating
key_terms.يَدِ: the hand, the affected limb in question
key_terms.يَمْسَحَ: to wipe, referring to the act of masḥ in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: it suffices him or is legally adequate for him

ai.seo_question: Is it sufficient in wudu (ablution) to wipe over a medicinal coating on the hand?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning wudu (ablution) when medicine is applied to the hand. It states that if there is a coating of medicine on the hand, wiping over it is sufficient, indicating facilitation in ritual purity when direct wiping on the skin is obstructed.
